transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-06-30
- Start time: 15:00 UTC
- Duration: 48m
- Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Redwood CSM), Marta Ruiz (AcroData SRE), Devon Clarke (AcroData Backend), Liam O'Connor (AcroData Product)

Summary:
Quick RCA walkthrough of the 06/28 surge that produced intermittent 5xxs/timeouts; alignment on retry/backoff policy; plan for targeted soak + logs; confirm fallback routing for VPC/private edge.

Topics:
- Root cause hypothesis: hot-keys + queue saturation + transient GPU kernel stalls
- Observed artifacts: 502/504 and occasional 500s, long tail latencies on token 2-4 for some streams
- Retry budget and client backoff strategy
- Fallbacks: cheaper quantized model or regional fallback vs degrade conversation length
- Next steps and ownership

Action items (read out):
- See action_items field for owners/dates.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: ok uh hi everyone thanks for joining, let's do a quick roll call, we have Marta, Devon, Liam from AcroData and Priya and Samir from Redwood. can you hear me fine?
[00:12] Marta: yeah loud and clear thanks Jordan, and we got devon here too.
[00:16] Devon: hey all.
[00:18] Priya: hi team, Priya on the SE side. I pulled a first-pass RCA and some flamegraphs.
[00:25] Jordan: great, goal for today is to align on root cause from the 06/28 incident and agree a short plan for retries and a soak. Marta can you summarize what you saw on your side?
[00:36] Marta: sure, so during the spike we saw a sharp jump in 95/99 tail, and the error mix was mostly 502 and 504 with some 500s. the errors were concentrated on two routes: /generate-chat and /embed-bulk. the interesting bit was request counts for certain user IDs spiking. looked like hot key behavior, and also we saw queue depth on our side increase even though client retries were modest.
[01:02] Jordan: when you say queue depth, is that per-tenant queue at the loadbalancer or within the Redwood runtime?
[01:08] Marta: both actually. load balancer pushed more requests to our VPC endpoint which then got queued at the shard frontdoor. on the Redwood side we saw a backlog metric increase and some workers reported long CPU libnv kernel wait, or that's how it surfaced in the traces, might be GPU kernel contention but the transcription on the trace called it 'lib n v' so not exact.
[01:31] Priya: yeah i saw the same in the flamegraphs -- KV cache warmup was poor for those hot keys, so cold cache meant longer early token times; combine that with a short client timeout and you get cascading retries which amplify the queue.
[01:44] Devon: quick q, were the retries exponential on the client? our SDK default is linear backoff with 200ms increments unless configured.
[01:52] Marta: right, our SDK was doing 3 retries with fixed 200ms backoff. we pushed a spike of concurrent sessions from a marketing event and a handful of users were hitting high qps.
[02:02] Jordan: ok that matches the hypothesis: hot-key induced cold-KV plus fixed small backoff creates thundering herd. Priya, what's your take on the 502 vs 504 split?
[02:12] Priya: 504s correlate with the request hitting the edge timeout — usually the gateway closed the connection when token generation exceeded 3.5s for that route. 502s were internal proxy errors when the worker crashed or returned malformed chunk. a few 500s came from out-of-memory on a small worker node during peak. again, not all observations are perfect because the traces had some missing spans.
[02:33] Liam: is there any sign this was model-quality related or only infra? our product team cares if the model caused long decoding times for certain prompts.
[02:41] Priya: we sampled some payloads — mostly long context + heavy few-shot prompts. that's higher compute per request, but the big multiplier was repeated requests from same session (no KV reuse early on). so primarily infra and request shape, not model correctness.
[02:55] Jordan: ok, so mitigation split: client side (retry/backoff, jitter, reduce retries), runtime config (prefill/warm KV, quota for hot keys, per-key rate limiting), and infra (autoscale thresholds, worker sizing, prevent OOM).
[03:09] Marta: can Redwood adjust the per-tenant shard fallback so that when a shard crosses a queue depth threshold it routes to quantized variant? that would avoid 5xxs while preserving service.
[03:19] Priya: yes, we can. Redwood routing supports model variants and we can set a policy: when queue_depth > X for Y seconds, route to quantized-3bit variant in same region. downside is some latency improvement but potential quality delta.
[03:33] Devon: what's the expected latency delta for the quantized fallback?
[03:36] Priya: in our internal tests quantized-3bit reduces per-token time by ~20-30% on tail, but you may see some increased repetition or slight quality shift on long-form outputs. depends on your prompt.
[03:48] Liam: we'd prefer graceful degrade over errors, so fallback is attractive. we just want to measure user-visible delta. can we run an A/B run?
[03:56] Jordan: yes we'll schedule a controlled canary — route 5% of traffic during a soak.
[03:59] Marta: sounds good.
[04:02] Jordan: next, retry policy. current customer SDK does 3 fixed retries at 200ms. Priya, recommend?
[04:09] Priya: recommend reducing client retries to 1-2 and add exponential backoff with jitter; e.g. initial 200ms * 2^n and random jitter up to 50%, max retry cap 2s. also add idempotency tokens for non-idempotent endpoints where possible. but also we should add server-side retry budget signals to reject bursts.
[04:27] Devon: what about adaptive throttles or token buckets? we saw a short-lived marketing event that created very bursty traffic, so a windowed throttle could smooth that.
[04:37] Priya: agree, a short token-bucket per-tenant with refill rate tuned to your baseline QPS will smooth spikes. Redwood has rate-windowing where we can set a per-route window and a burst multiplier; we'll propose baseline numbers after we see your traffic histogram.
[04:51] Marta: i'll share the histogram. we also noticed repeated 5xx with request ids that had large embeddings payloads; maybe clients are pushing batch sizes beyond recommended.
[04:59] Jordan: good point — we'll check batch limits. Priya, is there a quick server-side guard we can apply for oversized payloads?
[05:06] Priya: we can set a soft limit and return 413-like responses earlier with clear guidance; or apply a probabilistic sampler to reject extreme batch sizes during bursts to protect the service.
[05:17] Devon: that would help.
[05:19] Jordan: ok going into the RCA timeline we pulled spans for 06/28 14:12–14:42 UTC. Priya, walk through key trace snippets.
[05:28] Priya: first snippet shows request r-983: time to first token was 220ms normally, but during the spike we saw >1200ms because KV fetch fell back to disk for that key, and then the token generation had an internal retry in the runtime. second snippet r-1012 showed worker OOM in one container leading to a proxy 502. both snippets are attached in my notes.
[05:50] Marta: question — is that KV miss because of cold-start after scale-up or eviction?
[05:56] Priya: looks like eviction. the memory manager freed slots due to a larger batch allocation pattern; we need to tune the eviction policy for hot keys and consider warming strategies when we scale up.
[06:07] Jordan: is there a quick config change we can do that helps immediately?
[06:11] Priya: short-term: increase the KV cache high-water mark for your tenant by 20% and enable aggressive prefetch for hot keys for the soak. also set a shard queue depth threshold and fallback route.
[06:24] Jordan: we'll apply that in the soak. Marta, can you confirm you are comfortable with Redwood increasing the tenant cache quota temporarily?
[06:29] Marta: yes for the soak period, please monitor.
[06:31] Liam: when you say tenant cache quota, does that cost more?
[06:35] Jordan: temporarily, yes, it might bump resource usage; we'll surface expected cost delta in the follow-up note.
[06:41] Devon: about the SDK change — who will roll it? we can push a quick client patch to switch to exponential backoff.
[06:47] Marta: we can do that, but want Redwood to validate recommended parameters first.
[06:51] Jordan: action: Priya to propose concrete backoff params and policy doc; Marta to test client change in staging.
[06:58] Priya: sounds good.
[07:02] Samir: quick note, we'll also attach our standard SLO guidance doc and a recommended retry budget template.
[07:08] Jordan: thanks. now telemetry gaps: Marta you mentioned missing spans earlier. what's the visibility gap we need?
[07:15] Marta: some of the worker-level kernel events are not in the trace because the tracing wrapper isn't instrumented at the GPU kernel library level. we can add more verbose runtime logging but that will increase noise.
[07:26] Priya: agree, enable extra logging for the soak window only. we'll pull flamegraphs and aggregated kernel latency distributions.
[07:33] Devon: any security or compliance blockers for enabling deeper logs? we have PII in some prompts so we need to ensure logs are redacted.
[07:41] Jordan: Redwood supports redaction and KMS for log storage; we'll ensure logs are filtered and uploaded to your S3 endpoint with rotation. I'll share the security checklist.
[07:49] Marta: appreciated.
[07:52] Jordan: OK, experimental plan: 1) apply temporary KV high-water mark + prefetch; 2) set shard queue-dept threshold and route to quantized fallback when exceeded; 3) coordinate client SDK change to exponential backoff; 4) run 2-hour soak with a 5% canary for fallback and capture flamegraphs. Priya will run the soak and share logs.
[08:16] Priya: timeline wise i can kick off the soak tomorrow evening in our staging cluster or we can run it in your dedicated test slice, whichever you prefer.
[08:26] Marta: prefer in our dedicated test slice that mirrors prod. we'll share creds for the test slice ephemeral token.
[08:33] Jordan: Samir will coordinate the credentials exchange.
[08:36] Samir: i will share a one-time link after this call.
[08:40] Liam: about metrics, what should we watch during the soak?
[08:43] Priya: monitor: per-shard queue depth, TTF (time to first token), token tail p99/p995, KV hit rate for hot keys, OOM events, 5xx count, and end-to-end client retry counts.
[08:55] Devon: can Redwood produce a short dashboard template we can import?
[08:58] Priya: yes we'll export a dashboard and a Grafana JSON.
[09:02] Jordan: let's talk fallback quality validation — we'll instrument a prompt set and compute BLEU-ish or embedding-drift vs baseline, plus sample human checks. Liam, will product own the user-visible metric?
[09:14] Liam: yes, we'll own baseline sampling and set an acceptability threshold.
[09:18] Marta: and we'll tie rollout to the rate of 5xxs dropping below 1% of baseline.
[09:23] Jordan: sounds good.
[09:26] Priya: one more operational note: set a server-side short-circuit for oversized batches to protect memory, and a probabilistic early reject at 0.5% sample to measure impact.
[09:36] Devon: ok.
[09:38] Jordan: any questions from the customer team?
[09:40] Marta: just one — can Redwood share a short runbook for incident escalation if this recurs?
[09:45] Jordan: yes we'll share a runbook with triage steps, logs to pull, who to escalate to, and contact points. Samir will attach that to the follow-up.
[09:56] Samir: noted, will attach.
[09:58] Jordan: wrapping up — recap next steps: Priya run soak + share logs; Jordan share security checklist and cost delta; Marta share traffic histograms and request samples; Samir share creds and runbook.
[10:15] Marta: thanks everyone.
[10:18] Devon: thanks.
[10:20] Liam: cheers.
[10:22] Jordan: thanks all, we'll follow up in email with calendar invite for the canary window.
